stories.body: Ukraine is hosting British, French and German leaders for a meeting of the Coalition of the Willing as Russian attacks intensify and Kyiv reports a severe shortage of air-defence interceptors. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham is expected to announce that the United Kingdom will permit the declassification of information on Storm Shadow missile components to support Ukrainian production of long-range weapons, alongside French-backed assembly plans. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine needs hundreds of Patriot missiles for the winter and is pursuing additional systems and interceptors from the United States, France and Germany.
stories.headline: European leaders meet in Kyiv as Ukraine seeks urgent air-defence support

stories.body: Iran’s parliament has advanced draft legislation that would charge ships from countries permitted to pass through the Strait of Hormuz for services provided by Tehran. The move comes as the United States prepares additional sanctions and Iranian officials warn that countries joining Washington’s economic campaign will be treated as enemies. Iran’s security leadership has said that, if regional states cooperate with US restrictions, Gulf oil exports could be disrupted, including through routes intended to bypass the strategic waterway.
stories.headline: Iran advances Strait of Hormuz fee plans amid escalating US economic pressure

stories.body: Trade negotiations between the United States and Canada have collapsed, prompting Washington to impose 50% tariffs on roughly $20 billion in Canadian imports and Prime Minister Mark Carney to promise matching measures from 8 September. The US levies cover products including dairy, wine, clothing, construction materials and hockey equipment, while Canada plans tariffs on sectors including steel, appliances and electronics. Both governments blame the other for late changes in negotiations, deepening uncertainty over their highly integrated trading relationship and the future of the USMCA pact.
stories.headline: US-Canada trade talks collapse as both sides impose new tariffs

stories.body: The Democratic Republic of Congo and the Rwanda-backed AFC/M23 rebel group have agreed a roadmap for peace negotiations after five days of talks in Switzerland. The parties committed to pursue a comprehensive settlement under a US-brokered framework, establish timelines and create a mechanism to monitor alleged ceasefire violations, with a first verification mission planned in South Kivu. Major disagreements remain over sanctions against M23, detainees and political reforms, while fighting continues in eastern Congo despite repeated ceasefire commitments.
stories.headline: DR Congo and M23 rebels agree roadmap for renewed peace negotiations

stories.body: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has reached 5,515 confirmed cases and 2,642 deaths, according to government figures, making it the country’s deadliest recorded outbreak. The Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccine or treatment, and its reported fatality rate has risen to nearly 48%. Response efforts in Ituri and North Kivu are being hindered by conflict, displacement, attacks on medical workers and weak infrastructure, although contact tracing has improved. The World Health Organization has sent vaccine doses that may provide some protection and says the response must be significantly expanded.
stories.headline: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo surpasses 5,500 confirmed cases

stories.body: Syria’s foreign minister has met an Israeli delegation in Jordan in US-mediated talks aimed at reducing tensions after an Israeli strike on a Syrian airbase near the Turkish border. The discussions focused on halting Israeli attacks and arrests, reviving negotiations for a lasting security arrangement, and preventing Israeli-Turkish rivalry from spilling into Syria. Damascus reiterated its demand for Israeli forces to return to pre-2024 positions and for restoration of the 1974 disengagement agreement, while Israel reportedly maintained conditions involving Turkish military activity, demilitarisation near the Golan Heights and Syrian weapons capabilities.
stories.headline: Syria and Israel hold US-mediated talks in Jordan to reduce tensions

stories.body: A human-caused wildfire near Reno, Nevada, has destroyed homes, injured at least six people and forced thousands of residents to evacuate as shifting winds complicate firefighting efforts. The Hawk Fire began as a brushfire on Saturday and spread rapidly across the Peavine Peak area of the Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest, growing beyond 23 square miles with no containment reported. Authorities declared an emergency and urged as many as 90,000 people to leave threatened areas, while state and federal crews work to keep the fire from residential neighborhoods.
stories.headline: Fast-moving Nevada wildfire prompts major evacuations near Reno

stories.body: The Trump administration says Medicaid will stop covering gender-affirming surgeries and hormone treatments for transgender minors, while the Children’s Health Insurance Program will no longer cover the treatments for people under 19. The policy would continue mental-health coverage and phase out hormone treatment for current recipients by April 2027. LGBTQ+ advocates said the change would be challenged in court, arguing it interferes with families’ medical decisions, while the administration said it was intended to prevent federal funding for procedures it considers harmful.
stories.headline: Medicaid to end coverage for some gender-affirming care for transgender minors

stories.body: A federal judge has barred Idaho from prosecuting doctors who perform abortions to protect a pregnant patient’s health or prevent self-harm. Judge B. Lynn Winmill ruled that provisions of the state’s near-total abortion bans violate the Fourteenth Amendment because they distinguish between life-saving care and care intended to prevent serious but nonfatal harm. Idaho’s attorney general said the state will appeal. The ruling follows a challenge by a maternal-fetal medicine specialist who said the laws had forced patients with severe complications to travel out of state for treatment.
stories.headline: Federal judge blocks Idaho prosecutions over health-protecting abortions

stories.body: Authorities in Washington County, Oregon, are investigating the deaths of five people found on a rural property near Forest Grove, west of Portland, as a suspected quintuple homicide. Deputies initially responded to reports of a vehicle fire early Saturday and later discovered the victims’ remains and several dead domestic animals. Investigators said they do not believe the violence was random, but no arrests have been made and officials have not released the victims’ identities, causes of death or possible connections.
stories.headline: Five bodies found on rural Oregon property in suspected quintuple homicide

stories.body: Spain’s government is preparing for a series of parliamentary appearances by seven ministers as the unresolved migration crisis in Ceuta dominates the start of the political season. The government says it will present verified information about the mass arrival of migrants at the end of July, while the opposition accuses it of avoiding scrutiny in the Senate. Thousands of migrants, including many unaccompanied minors, remain in the autonomous city, intensifying disputes over transfers to mainland Spain, relations with Morocco, public-health conditions and responsibility for the emergency.
stories.headline: Ceuta migration and public-health crisis dominates Spain’s political return

stories.body: Spain’s health ministry has called an urgent meeting with regional authorities to secure vaccines for migrants remaining in Ceuta after the mass arrival from Morocco. The ministry is seeking doses for diseases including measles, chickenpox, polio, tetanus and diphtheria. Opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo has urged the government to consider isolating people with infectious diseases, citing reported cases of tuberculosis, scabies, gastroenteritis and chickenpox, while Health Minister Mónica García said public-health responsibilities in Ceuta are shared with the city’s government and surveillance systems are active.
stories.headline: Spain seeks vaccines for Ceuta as opposition urges isolation of infectious cases

stories.body: A Stanford research project published in Science has raised fresh biosecurity concerns after researchers used genomic AI models to design 16 new bacteriophages capable of infecting E. coli. The viruses were engineered under laboratory safety controls and cannot infect animal cells, but the researchers warned that comparable methods could potentially produce viruses that infect cells if used in other contexts. Experts say the technology could support medical applications, such as highly targeted cancer-fighting viruses, while also creating risks that require stronger governance, containment standards and security review.
stories.headline: AI-designed viruses raise new biosecurity concerns

stories.body: Spain’s meteorological agency has warned of strong to very strong storms, potentially large hail and powerful wind gusts across the Iberian System, Ebro Valley, Navarre, the Basque Country, the Pyrenees and eastern Castilla-La Mancha. Intense downpours are also possible along parts of the Mediterranean coast, while a front is expected to bring rain to Galicia. In Catalonia, civil-protection authorities have maintained the Inuncat alert for heavy rain, warning that some areas could receive more than 20 litres per square metre in 30 minutes and urging people to avoid rivers, flood-prone areas and unnecessary travel.
stories.headline: Storm and hail alerts issued across northern and eastern Spain

stories.body: Catalonia’s Civil Protection agency has kept the Inuncat emergency plan at alert level ahead of expected intense rain in the northwest, Pyrenees, Pre-Pyrenees and interior regions. Forecasts warn that rainfall could exceed 20 litres per square metre in 30 minutes, with some mountain areas potentially receiving much larger totals, and that storms may bring hail, strong gusts and sudden downbursts. Barcelona is expected to see more clouds, wind and scattered showers, while the heaviest conditions are forecast elsewhere in the region. Authorities have urged residents to avoid flood-prone routes, riverbeds and unnecessary travel during downpours.
stories.headline: Catalonia remains on alert for intense rain and storms

stories.body: Barcelona taxi drivers say severe traffic congestion around the city’s cruise terminals has caused some passengers to miss ships and flights despite leaving with ample time. The jams are concentrated near Plaça de les Drassanes, the Ronda Litoral and the Porta d’Europa bridge leading to the Adossat pier, especially on weekends and Sundays when several cruise ships depart. Élite Taxi Barcelona says waits to enter or leave the port have sometimes exceeded three hours and that port authorities have yet to provide an effective solution.
stories.headline: Barcelona taxi drivers warn port congestion is making cruise passengers miss departures

stories.body: Catalonia’s left-wing Comuns party has filed a complaint with the Generalitat over a demonstration by the Save Europe Act movement in Barcelona’s Plaça de Sant Jaume. The party says the gathering, attended by just over 50 people, promoted an exclusionary European ethnic identity and discriminated against non-white people and migrants. Comuns has asked the Office for Equal Treatment and Non-Discrimination to impose a serious penalty on organisers and spokespersons and to refer the matter to prosecutors if there is evidence of hate-crime offences.
stories.headline: Catalonia’s Comuns file complaint over xenophobic Barcelona demonstration
